prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The five frames show a bed or couch extending across the foreground, about 0.4–1.2 m from the camera wearer, with a small white animal roughly 0.5–1.3 m ahead and the wearer’s arm reaching in from the right or lower-right. Brighter depth values separate the nearby forearm, hand, animal, and final close-up paw from the darker wall and background; across frames, the animal shifts from the upper-left/left to near center, then lower-right, while the hand remains within roughly 0.2–0.7 m and appears to approach it. The map makes front-to-back layering clearer than RGB, including the arm lying in front of the animal in the first two frames and the animal standing above the furniture surface in frame 3. Absolute distances are uncertain, boundaries bleed around the animal and hand, and the bright diagonal structure at the top of frame 3 appears depth-inconsistent or partly out of view.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation identifies the supporting furniture as a bed in frame 1 and a couch in frame 3, the camera wearer’s visible arms or hands as person instances, and the small animal as dog in frame 3; no separate full person is visible, so facing direction or gaze cannot be established. Its masks clarify left/right occupancy and overlap: the wearer’s arm enters from the right toward the animal on the left in frames 1–2, the animal is centered and partly overlapped by the hand in frame 3, and only partial hands or arms remain near the lower-right in frames 4–5. The hand and animal are within approximately arm’s reach of each other—about 0–0.5 m apart—while both lie roughly 0.3–1.3 m from the camera. The map is unreliable across time: the animal and furniture disappear in frames 2, 4, and 5, the animal’s class label may be wrong, and large black regions include both true background and missed objects, so depth ordering and metric distance cannot be recovered from segmentation alone.
descriptions.pose: The pose map isolates articulated geometry that is difficult to trace in RGB: yellow body joints and magenta hand skeletons place the wearer’s forearm and hand in front of the camera in frame 3 and near the lower-right in frame 4, with a larger close hand at the right in frame 5. The hand moves from near the upper-center in frame 3 to lower-right in frame 4 and then remains on the right at closer apparent scale in frame 5, indicating a downward/rightward motion followed by approach; the mapped limbs are roughly 0.2–0.8 m from the camera and within arm’s reach of the nearby animal. No other complete human body, face, head orientation, or gaze is resolved, and the animal, furniture, and room layout are absent from this map, so their positions require RGB context. The pose estimate is unreliable because frames 1–2 contain no skeleton, the body chain is fragmentary, some joints float without a visible connecting limb, and the hand outlines can be displaced or incomplete under occlusion and image-edge cropping.
